steps.hook: POV: you laugh at a joke you didn't hear and hope no one noticed.

steps.alt_text: Man silent while others around him talk dark cinematic. Overlay text r...

steps.caption:
That fake laugh isn't you being dishonest. It's you choosing embarrassment later over exposure now.
Your nervous system decided that asking twice would confirm you're slow, so it made you nod and laugh on cue. It's not about the joke. It's about not giving the group another reason to clock you as different.
If you rewind that empty laugh for hours after everyone else forgot the punchline, you're not alone.
Comment HEARD and I'll send you the full breakdown.

steps.hook: POV: your phone rings and you watch it ring until it stops.

steps.alt_text: Man alone holding phone looking at it dark room cinematic. Overlay tex...

steps.caption:
That missed call wasn't you being rude. It was your body shutting down before you could even say hello.
Your nervous system reads a ringing phone as a trial with no script and no face to read. Just your voice, exposed. So it freezes you first, then punishes you with guilt for freezing.
If you let calls ring out and text back like you just saw it, you're not alone. You're not ignoring people. You're trying to survive a moment that feels like being seen too closely.
